actor: owner or manager of low-utilization physical/public assets
observed_state: assets can remain vacant, low-utilization, fragmented, misconfigured for current demand, or trapped in static administrative use
observed_change: multiple Chinese jurisdictions are shifting toward marketized operation, functional repurposing, digital asset management, public leasing and professional operation
hidden_or_underrecognized_value: the same underlying asset can create higher utility or revenue when its permissible use, operator, tenant, service scenario or transaction channel is changed
why_value_is_not_recognized_or_realized: asset information is fragmented; rights, approvals and operating responsibility are unclear; scenario fit is not obvious; transaction and operating workflows are costly to coordinate
complementary_actor_hypothesis: professional operators, transaction platforms, service providers and end users can absorb or transform assets that the owner cannot efficiently activate alone
complementary_actor_state: counterpart actors have operating capability, tenant/user demand, transaction infrastructure or specialist conversion capability but do not automatically see every stranded asset
transformation_mechanism: standardize asset facts and constraints, identify permissible scenario changes, match operator/user/transaction route, define acceptance and compliance rules, then execute leasing, operation, repurposing or disposal
why_exchange_does_not_already_happen: information asymmetry, rights ambiguity, fragmented approval, weak packaging, missing operator capability, low market visibility and transaction/compliance friction
incremental_value_for_origin_actor: higher utilization, rent/operating income, reduced vacancy, disposal proceeds, lower management leakage or public-service value
incremental_value_for_complementary_acto: access to usable space/assets, operating revenue, transaction/service fees, capacity expansion or user-service scenarios
orchestrator_value_capture_hypothesis: only if evidence later proves a repeatable bounded service, the orchestrator could be paid through management fees, transaction/service fees or a transparent share of incremental value created
cheapest_decisive_validation: in Xuzhou/Jiangsu, obtain 5-10 current stranded-asset cases from independent owners and verify whether the same intake, constraint classification, scenario matching and operator-routing steps recur; separately verify at least two accepted paid mandates
kill_conditions: cases remain one-off bespoke political/administrative projects; no independent owner will pay for or delegate the process; rights/approval constraints dominate; market counterparties are already efficiently connected; or every case requires unrelated bespoke transformation

evidence.claim: IDLE_ASSET_SCENARIO_REPURPOSING reached PROMOTION_REVIEW_READY from multiple actors, sources and periods without canonical taxonomy promotion.
A state-owned asset owner procures an external professional operator for recurring asset management and operation services.
Entrusted asset operation requires explicit agreements and standardized responsibilities for maintenance, rent/property-fee collection and invoicing, showing real coordination/compliance boundaries.
Repeated executed leases, operating-right transactions and disposals demonstrate realized value once assets reach market channels.

Entrusted asset operation requires explicit agreements and standardized responsibilities for maintenance, rent/property-fee collection and invoicing, showing that moving an asset into active use depends on a defined rights-and-operating interface rather than simple discovery alone.

State-owned asset rental is routed through a standardized platform with structured asset intake and explicit entrustment arrangements, evidencing recurring fragmentation that must be normalized before assets can be exposed to market counterparties.

surface_phenomenon_or_friction: Existing physical/public assets repeatedly remain vacant, low-utilization or mismatched to current use while owners and governments repeatedly inspect, repackage, lease, entrust, repurpose or marketize them through separate processes.
latent_outcome_hypothesis: Move an already-owned asset into a materially higher-utilization, revenue-producing or service-producing state without requiring the owner to build a new asset or personally operate every possible use scenario.
structural_friction_hypothesis: The asset is not natively callable as a permissioned, constraint-explicit, acceptance-ready operating unit: facts, rights, approvals, operating responsibility, tenant/operator fit and transaction workflow remain fragmented across administrative and market interfaces, so a potentially useful asset cannot be reconfigured and routed cheaply or repeatedly.
alternative_explanations: Low utilization may be caused mainly by weak end-user demand, poor location or intrinsically low asset quality rather than fragmented rights, packaging and operating interfaces.
Observed public/SOE activation mechanisms may be policy-specific and may not generalize to private owners or to an independent paid orchestration role.
